'''Abell Cauthon''' is a farmer and horse trader from [[Emond's Field]] in the [[Two Rivers]].{{ref/book|3|19}} He is married to [[Natti Cauthon]] and they have three children: [[Matrim Cauthon|Matrim]], [[Eldrin Cauthon|Eldrin]] and [[Bodewhin Cauthon|Bodewhin]]. Abell serves on the [[Village Council]] of Emond's Field.{{ref/book|4|53}}

== Appearance & Abilities ==
By {{ne|998}} Abell was middle-aged and resembled an older, graying version of his son [[Matrim Cauthon]]. He is well known as being an expert with both the quarterstaff and the [[Two Rivers Longbow]].{{ref/book|3|24}} Abell is also widely regarded as being the finest horse trader in the Two Rivers; always seemingly able to secure a superior trade with either outlander merchants or [[Taren Ferry]] men.{{ref/book|3|24}}

== History ==
Abell was born near Emond's Field in {{ne|955}} to a family of farmers. He spent his youth in and around the Emond's Field area and became well knowledgeable of the terrain of the [[Westwood]] and the [[Waterwood]]. He married his wife Natti circa {{ne|975}} and settled in the middle of the Emond's Field village where he raised five children.

== Activities ==
Sometime after Rand, Mat, Perrin and the others left Emond's Field, he journeyed to Tar Valon with Tam al'Thor to find out what happened to his son and the others.{{ref/book|3|20}}{{ref/book|4|31}}

When [[Perrin Aybara]] comes home to Emond's Field, [[Marin al'Vere]] tells him that Abell and [[Tam al'Thor]] managed to escape when the [[Children of the Light|Whitecloaks]] arrested Abell's family and the Luhhan's, and that they are hiding somewhere in the Westwood.{{ref/book|4|29}} Her husband says that [[Padan Fain]] has offered two hundred pieces of gold for Tam and Abell. The Whitecloaks have also burned Abell's house.

During the fighting with [[Trolloc]]s in Emond's Field, Abell shows himself to be a very capable fighter and he and Tam help Perrin with the planning on more than one occasion.

He participates in the [[Battle of Emond's Field]].{{ref/book|4|56}}

Abell becomes one of the commanding officers in Perrin's army. The officers discuss with [[Elayne Trakand]] information gathered from all the war-fronts.


==Parallels==
Abell Cauthon's name derives not from the Biblical story of Cain and Abel, but from Sir Ebel, a knight in Malory who plays a role in the story of Sir Palamides.{{ref|[[Origins of the Wheel of Time]], Abell Cauthon}}

==In the television series==
* In the [[The Wheel of Time (TV series)|TV series]], {{TVlink|Abell Cauthon}} is played by actor {{TVlink|Christopher Sciueref}}.
